body:
I've run into this before. Batch processing queues are subtly difficult. The only way I have been able to get this kind of code to work is by hiding all the locking functionality and creating a new abstraction (let me know if you find issues I can fix, this particular pair of classes hasn't got any real testing yet):

[StateWatcher.java](https://github.com/Telenav/kivakit/blob/develop/kivakit-kernel/src/main/java/com/telenav/kivakit/kernel/language/threading/conditions/StateWatcher.java)
[StateMachine.java](https://github.com/Telenav/kivakit/blob/develop/kivakit-kernel/src/main/java/com/telenav/kivakit/kernel/language/threading/conditions/StateMachine.java)

I made a few changes to this code so you might be able to use or adapt it:

[Batcher.java](https://github.com/Telenav/kivakit/blob/develop/kivakit-kernel/src/main/java/com/telenav/kivakit/kernel/language/threading/batcher/Batcher.java)

This one is pretty serious now. With the improvements to ILM which trigger a much higher rate of ILM task completion than previously possible, this reproduces a deadlock in our many shards benchmarking reliably after a couple of hours.

issue.title: Get hot threads on lagging nodes

labels.name: :Distributed/Cluster Coordination
labels.description: Cluster formation and cluster state publication, including cluster membership and fault detection.

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
When the master removes a node from the cluster with reason `lagging`
it's often germane to ask what the node was doing that prevented it from
applying cluster states quickly enough. Frequently it's waiting on slow
IO, or else doing something very expensive on the applier thread. This
commit adds an automatic call to the hot threads API on the lagging node
so that the master can log extra detail about what it's busy doing if
`DEBUG` logging is enabled.

issue.body:
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/68468 and also to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/80522 (this is a cleaned up and much-more-reviewable version of most of the latter).

Besides some test cleanups, the primary thrust of this PR is the final commit it changes the ILMHistoryStore flush policy. It was count and size (and time) based, but the size was unlikely to ever trigger (these objects are generally in the neighborhood of 512 bytes or thereabouts, so one hundred of them would never be even close to 5MB).

This changes it to being size (and time) based, and setting that size to 50MB. For most clusters, this will mean it's now *time* based (5s).

issue.title: Deadlock related to `BulkProcessor` used by deprecation logger indexing appender

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

many, but observed in 8.1.3

### Installed Plugins

N/A

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

Cloud

### Problem Description

The deprecation logger indexes documents using `BulkProcessor#add` on the thread which encountered the use of the deprecated feature. This could be any thread, and may in particular be a `generic` one. This means it is susceptible to the same kind of deadlock as in #68468: if all the `generic` threads try and emit deprecation logs at the same time then they will all block and wait in vain for a `generic` thread to become available to actually do the indexing.

### Steps to Reproduce

This should be possible to reproduce if there is more concurrent deprecation logging than the number of generic threads. In the case in which it was observed, the generic threads were in fact all blocked by #68468, but deprecation logging on a `transport_worker` thread caused this thread to join the pile-up.

issue.title: Do not hold the lock during flush in BulkProcessor

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
This commit releases the BulkProcessor lock after a new bulk request
is created during flush instead of waiting until the request is
dispatched. This prevents a deadlock when the GENERIC thread pool
is saturated with tasks adding new items to the BulkProcessor
waiting to obtain the lock, this might prevent the original
BulkRequest of making progress in certain scenarios, as some
retry operations might be dispatched in the GENERIC thread pool.

Closes #68468

body: Bump to see if any movement can be made here. This one can negatively affect clusters in ESS and make things difficult to operate/fix.
@jaymode we discussed this a bit more today within the DM team and @joegallo is going to have a look at https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/86862 to try to move it along.
